name: Virgin Records
ownershipStory: Grew out of a record shop into an independent label built on Mike Oldfield's 'Tubular Bells' (1973), then expanded aggressively into punk and post-punk while staying independent. Branson sold Virgin Records to Thorn EMI in 1992; the label continues to operate today as part of Universal Music Group.
hook: Started as a record shop and became big enough to sign punk's aftermath without blinking.

blurb.age7: Virgin started as a record shop and grew into a record company big enough to release Public Image Ltd's strange music.
blurb.age13: Richard Branson and his partners started Virgin as a record shop, then a label, and its first release, Mike Oldfield's 'Tubular Bells,' made it rich enough to take chances on stranger music later, including John Lydon's post-punk band Public Image Ltd.
blurb.adult: Virgin's trajectory from scrappy independent to major label happened fast, largely on the back of 'Tubular Bells,' and by the time it signed Public Image Ltd in 1978 it had the resources to release genuinely difficult music (Metal Box's unusual packaging among them) at real commercial scale. Branson sold the label to Thorn EMI in 1992.
